spec.name: News tone v13
spec.notes: Long names with improving news sentiment.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.0, annual return 3%, maximum drawdown 6%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 0.97 to 0.75 (change -0.22).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 0.97 to 0.97. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 0.97 (as submitted, 10 bps: 0.97); it breaks even at 30.4 bps with daily turnover 0.06.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 0.97 against 0.97 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 0.91 against 0.97 in research, a gap of +0.06.
The best year gives 79% of total P&L (year 7) and calm regimes give 44%; Sharpe is 0.81 in calm and 1.62 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.09, so the claimed 1.00 becomes 0.91 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.45 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.01, 95th percentile 0.54).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 0.97 to as low as 0.69 (as low as 0.76 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 109% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 65% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Paper trading only: soft test damaging (regime_split EX-6, day_concentration EX-10).
